notes:
Summary: Mid-market product org building in-app assistant and knowledge search. Started on hosted API for speed-to-value, now moving to Dedicated for predictable unit economics and isolation. Key asks: committed capacity level that matches peak-with-burst, clear ramp schedule, pre-negotiated overage rate, and VPC connectivity + SOC2 audit artifacts.

POC results (internal): - Hosted API was easy to integrate; steady-state costs higher than internal target. - With early batching/caching suggestions from SE, token costs dropped ~35% and QoL improved.

Procurement/Technical details: - Target throughput: sustained 40-60 requests/sec (chat+embedding mix), peak bursts up to 120 req/sec for marketing events. - Latency target: p95 < 300ms on 512-token contexts for chat; embeddings up to 500ms acceptable. - Preferred model family: open variants comparable to gpt-4-qualifiers; care about rerouting to smaller variants for cost savings. - Data handling: VPC peering required, keys in customer KMS, audit log retention 12 months.

Pricing/Packaging talk (notes from 2/21 workshop): - Interested in a 12-month reserved commit with 3-month ramp: month1=40% commit, month2=70%, month3=100%. - Need clear burst rules: allow 2x burst over commit for up to 48 hours/month; negotiate flat burst fee or credits. - Overage: prefer pre-approved overage with capped per-token overage rate (goal: <= 1.5x committed unit price). - Want examples: show modeled bill with our traffic curve and compare hosted vs dedicated 12-months.

Quotes / customer voice: - "We want predictable bills — last quarter spike killed our dev budget." — Head of Product, Maya Chen.

Open items for Redwood: - Provide SOW draft with explicit commit definition (GPU hours vs throughput), burst policy language, overage cap examples, and a modeled 12-month cost scenario for Hartwell's POC traffic. - Provide SOC2 artifact packet + SSO integration timeline. - Confirm region parity for VPC peering (us-east and eu-west).
commercial_notes: Hartwell is price-sensitive but not commodity; willing to commit if we can demonstrate >=40% TCO improvement vs hosted and define simple burst/overage rules. They asked about 0-12 month ramp with credits for under-utilization in first 2 months.
